Looking at the bounding client rectangles provided:

The `root>plain>pin` element has `getBoundingClientRect: x=10 y=10 width=80 height=20`. The `getBoundingClientRect()` method returns coordinates relative to the viewport (not relative to any parent element).

Since `root>plain>pin` has `position: absolute` and `top: 10px; left: 10px`, it is positioned absolutely. Its parent `root>plain` has `position: static` (not positioned), so the absolutely positioned child is positioned relative to the nearest positioned ancestor, which is `root` (which has `position: relative`).

The bounding client rect gives us the actual rendered position in viewport coordinates: x=10, y=10 represents the top-left corner of the element as it appears on the screen.
